style_when: the story is about change after hours — automation displacing shifts, a market open all night, capacity running while people sleep
prompt: Architectural night photograph, 35mm lens at f/4, low-angle asymmetric composition: an unbranded modern heat pump condenser in a galvanised steel cabinet on a concrete pad along the driveway side of a suburban stucco house at deep blue hour, placed off-centre right with the two-storey wall and asphalt shingle roofline filling the left of frame. Deep slate grey ambient light falls from the left; warm ochre light spills outward from the kitchen windows, and higher up an attic gable vent glows the same amber, a faint plume of heated air bleeding into the cold night. Frost dusts the concrete, bone white trim, long calm exposure, fine film grain, no people.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, logos
rationale: The 'silent leak' happens at night, while the machine runs and the house sleeps — exactly the after-hours story architectural_night exists to tell. Blue-hour calm, lit windows as the only warm source, and a low-angle composition let the heat pump itself be the hero machine while the glowing attic vent carries the leak the quote never itemizes. Editorial_macro would strip the environment that makes the house-versus-duct conflict legible, and a document flat-lay could not carry the running machine at all.
subject: an unbranded heat pump condenser running on its concrete pad at blue hour while warm air bleeds from the attic vent above
core_thesis: A heat pump quoted at the 7.5 HSPF2 legal floor is the weakest machine you can legally install, and the unlabeled ductwork feeding it silently wastes more energy than the upgrade recovers.
core_conflict: The labeled, rated, itemized machine on the quote versus the unlabeled, uninspectable duct run in the attic — the only line with a label on it gets the money, while the hole in the system costs more than half of what the model upgrade saves.
composition: Low-angle asymmetric composition: condenser off-centre right in the foreground, the stucco wall and glowing asphalt-shingle roofline rising to fill the left of frame, generous dark sky above
